stories.title: MLB Hall of Fame Induction Day — Beltran, Jones, and Kent Enshrined at Cooperstown
stories.angle: The 2026 Baseball Hall of Fame induction ceremony takes place today at Clark Sports Center, Cooperstown — the first Sunday of HOF Weekend, July 24-27. Carlos Beltrán (Mets cap), Andruw Jones (Braves cap), and Jeff Kent (Giants cap) become the 346th, 347th, and 348th members of the Hall. A record 61 Hall of Famers are attending. Beltrán, a nine-time All-Star and three-time Gold Glover, was elected by BBWAA in his fourth try. Jones, who won 10 consecutive Gold Gloves with Atlanta, was elected in his ninth BBWAA try. Jeff Kent — the all-time leader in home runs by a second baseman (351 as a 2B, 377 career) and the 2000 NL MVP — was elected by the Contemporary Baseball Era Committee last December.

stories.title: Ohtani Setback — Skips Bullpen Session, Says Knee Still Not 100%
stories.angle: Shohei Ohtani was scheduled to throw a bullpen session Sunday at Citi Field. He did not. Manager Dave Roberts told reporters the session was skipped because of "regression" in the left knee — Ohtani had thrown approximately 30 pitches in a bullpen on July 22, but his most recent assessment showed he "just doesn't feel 100%." Roberts indicated Ohtani won't return to the mound until the knee is fully right. He has not pitched in a game since July 3 (8-2, 1.79 ERA, 95K in 85.2 IP). His return is now August at the earliest. He continues to DH and hit .288/.397/.536.

stories.title: Trade Deadline — Tigers Leaning Toward Keeping Skubal; Abrams, Miller Heating Up
stories.angle: Eight days to the August 3 deadline and the Tarik Skubal trade market is evolving. Detroit is now leaning toward keeping their two-time Cy Young winner — the Tigers have gone 25-15 since June 1 and are within striking distance in the AL Central. Multiple rival executives believe the Tigers will hold. Meanwhile: CJ Abrams (Nationals) is available — Yankees, Brewers, and Red Sox all have interest. Mason Miller (Padres closer) is the subject of conflicting reports — some believe a trade is inevitable, others say he stays. The Dodgers are aggressive buyers targeting a historic three-peat. Deadline is August 3 at 6 PM ET.

stories.title: Pete Crow-Armstrong Breaks the Statcast 5-Star Catch Record
stories.angle: Pete Crow-Armstrong owns the Statcast record for the most 5-star catches in history. The Chicago Cubs outfielder broke the previous record — held by Kevin Kiermaier — when he recorded his 33rd career five-star catch (a play with 25% or lower catch probability) on July 21. He got there in fewer opportunities than any other player in Statcast history. At 24 years old, having made his MLB debut in September 2023, PCA has surpassed every outfielder who came before him in this specific measure of defensive excellence. This is the best center fielder alive — and his offense is growing to match.

stories.title: Kyle Schwarber Leads MLB with 32 HR at 35 — On Pace for 60 Again
stories.angle: Kyle Schwarber is 35 years old and leading Major League Baseball in home runs with 32. Yordan Alvarez is second at 31. Ben Rice is third at 29. Schwarber led the NL with 56 home runs in 2025. At his current pace in 2026, he is on track to approach or surpass that number again. The Phillies' DH/left fielder is not supposed to be doing this at his age. Most power hitters peak in their mid-to-late 20s and decline through their 30s. Schwarber keeps hitting balls over fences at a rate that defies every historical pattern in the sport.
